issues.issue: "All precautions necessary to ensure against the creation, use, or storage of any hazardous material" is an absolute-sounding standard with no benchmark, and the second sentence limits compliance to "Environmental Protection Agency laws or regulations" only. Whether Ohio EPA/ORC obligations or common-law duties fall inside that phrase is open.

This narrow undertaking to comply with "Environmental Protection Agency laws or regulations" sits against paragraph 7.F, which requires conformity with all applicable federal, state and local laws, leaving Hardrives' environmental compliance duty stated at two different widths. A court would have to decide which measure governs contamination claims.

The indemnity covers claims "resulting from injury on or about the Premises or in conjunction with Hardrives' use and occupancy," without saying whether "injury" reaches environmental contamination and cleanup costs or only bodily/property injury, and without any carve-out for the City's own fault. Both the subject matter and the party protected are open to construction.

A broad indemnity running to the City is difficult to square with paragraph 6.D, in which the City warrants the environmental condition of the Premises, if the same contamination is both warranted against and indemnified. A court could be asked which provision allocates pre-existing contamination liability.

The general compliance covenant overlaps paragraph 7.D's narrower Environmental Protection Agency compliance obligation, and it is unclear whether the specific environmental clause qualifies this general one. The tension is mild but nameable.

The "as is" acceptance with no express or implied warranty is expressly subject to "warranties and representations made by the City ... contained in this Agreement," which include the paragraph 6.D environmental warranty; the two provisions point in opposite directions on the condition of the Premises. A court would have to decide how much of the as-is disclaimer survives paragraph 6.D.

The merger clause makes this Agreement and "the documents delivered pursuant hereto" the entire agreement, yet paragraph 5 conditions the term on a separate Development Agreement to be entered into later. Whether that later instrument is inside or outside the integration is a construction question.

The bar on assignment without written consent stands against paragraph 12, which extends the defined terms "City" and "Hardrives" to their "successors, and assigns." A court could be asked whether paragraph 12 contemplates assignees the assignment clause forbids.

The survival clause says warranties survive "the execution and delivery of this Agreement" but says nothing about surviving termination or expiry of the one-year term. Whether the City's environmental warranty remains enforceable after the licence ends is left open.

Including "assigns" within the defined parties is in tension with paragraph 9's prohibition on assignment without written consent. The definition appears to contemplate a class the operative clause bars.

A precise metes-and-bounds description of Parcel No. 3 is prefaced by "shall include, but is not limited to," so the survey does not close the definition of the Premises. A court would have to decide whether land outside the described bounds is licensed.

The 58.086-acre Parcel No. 3 described here does not match the "Parcel No. 3 (5.44 acre site)" assessed in the Exhibit B environmental report incorporated by paragraph 6.D. The two exhibits use the same parcel label for different land.

The excepted conveyances to CSX and Mahoning County sit against paragraph 6.B's warranty that the Premises is clear of all liens and claims and that no proceedings affect it, and against Exhibit A's "not limited to" language. Whether these exceptions qualify the City's warranty is left unstated.
